limits: Only the three returned Molawin Creek records with order Atheriniformes and family Phallostethidae were reviewed as fish candidates; the remaining records were grouped as Aves or Insecta.
GBIF's indexed locality field is text, not a waterbody polygon. No coordinate-only, spelling-variant or broader geographic search was performed.
The zero-result strings for Dampalit Falls and Cambantoc River do not establish species absence from either waterbody.

datasets.citation: Natural History Museum (2026). Natural History Museum (London) Collection Specimens. Occurrence dataset https://doi.org/10.5519/qd.dyj48ok9 accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-10-23.

decision.rationale: Three preserved-specimen records in two CC0 occurrence datasets independently carry the same GBIF taxon key and the same Molawin Creek locality string. The accepted name is confirmed in GBIF and the independent Catalog of Fishes. Collapse them to one species-waterbody assertion; record multiplicity is not abundance or a count of individuals.
caveats: All records lack event dates and coordinates; the 1933 text inside NHM catalog numbers is not interpreted as a collection date.
Two NHM records carry institution/collection matching flags. The CAS record carries continent-field and inferred-occurrence-status flags; no coordinate-based geographic validation is possible.
The locality is assigned by text only. No stream geometry, exact station, current presence, abundance, native status, catchability, legality, safety, diet or bait effect is asserted.

The separate 2011 Makiling article remains unextracted. NUS Digital Gems labels its copy Open Access, but its terms say that this label does not grant reuse and prohibit structured dataset extraction without explicit permission or an item license.

nonClaims: This is not a current-presence report or a complete fish inventory for Molawin Creek, Makiling or Laguna.
No species absence is inferred from the zero-result searches for Dampalit Falls or Cambantoc River.
The three occurrence records are not counted as three independent collection events or three individual fish.
